data.narrative:
Auterion, a Series B-stage defense and security software company founded by Lorenz Meier and Kevin Sartori, has raised $130M+ to date. The valuation analysis draws from a comparable universe of 10 peers—8 private firms and 2 public companies (DRSHF, IDEAFORGE.NS)—all operating in the Defense & Security sector at similar or comparable stages.

Two triangulation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis uses the $130M total raised as a valuation proxy, applying a 1.9x multiplier typical of Series B advancement, yielding $247M. Peer-median analysis examines 7 same-sector, same-stage private comparables including Dream Security ($3.0B), Harmattan AI ($1.4B), Code Metal ($1.2B), Castelion ($1.0B), and Defense Unicorns ($1.0B), establishing a median valuation of $1.0B with a range spanning $300M to $3.0B.

The two methods produce a triangulated valuation range of $210M (low) to $1.1B (high), with a median of $624M. This wide dispersion reflects material uncertainty around Auterion's positioning within the peer set. Key sensitivities include stage-of-readiness relative to $1B+ comparables, revenue scale relative to peers, and customer concentration in a sector where large contracts drive valuations. The stage-progression floor assumes limited differentiation; the peer median anchors to observable market pricing. Further due diligence on revenue, customer base, and technology defensibility would narrow this range.
